question.problem: Given the function $y=2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+3{e}^{x},$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+3{e}^{x}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{x}+3{e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{x}+3{e}^{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{2}{x}+3{e}^{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{1}+3{e}^{1} \\  & =2+3e\,.\end{aligned}
$$
